correctness.rationale: Both normalized densities integrate to one on their active intervals. For H=F−v, the continuous curve has H(0)=H(1)=0 and is strictly concave on each side of activation. Thus if H(d)≥0 there is no sign-changing interior zero; H(d)=0 makes a contact with H>0 on both sides. If H(d)<0, the strictly monotone secant slopes from each anchored endpoint give at most one interior zero per side, with existence exactly when the respective slope H′(0+)>0 or H′(1−)<0. Substitution gives w>L, w<U0 and w<U1. At w=L concavity at both anchored segments makes both slope inequalities strict, proving nonemptiness; L>0 follows from strict concavity of F1 and U0<1. U1 falls strictly from +∞ to 0 as d ranges from 0 to 1, and solving z=c+(1−c)/U0 gives the unique switch. Independent symbolic limits give (1−exp(−a))/2 for width/d at the initial end and a/2 for width/(1−d)^2 at the terminal end; the matched linear terms cancel at the latter. value.rationale: This is a motivated mechanism for nonmonotone cumulative mass surplus despite decreasing release within each source. The exact feasible weight window quantifies when a second crossing can occur and shows why estimation of the effect becomes far more sensitive as activation approaches the event end. Those are informative comparisons within a natural idealized model, not a prescription for capture-system design or a rediscovery of observed mixed curves.
